title: Etale-local lifts of scheme objects through a smooth stack covering family
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal X$ and $(\mathcal X_j)_{j\in J}$ be algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $(p_j:\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X)_{j\in J}$ be a set-indexed family of smooth morphisms, not necessarily representable. Smoothness is tested on smooth scheme charts, with scheme smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Assume the family is jointly surjective: every object of $\mathcal X$ over a field admits, after some extension of that field, an isomorphism to the image of an object of some $\mathcal X_j$; use the field-valued and chart conventions of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. For every $S$-scheme $U$ and object $x\in\mathcal X(U)$, there exist a set-indexed jointly surjective etale family $(e_i:U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-etale-morphism], indices $j(i)\in J$, objects $y_i\in\mathcal X_{j(i)}(U_i)$ and isomorphisms $p_{j(i)}(y_i)\simeq e_i^*x$ in $\mathcal X(U_i)$. Pullbacks, fibre groupoids and isomorphisms use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. All the covering schemes and objects lie in the chosen site universe. No quasi-compactness, separation, finite-type or Noetherian hypotheses are imposed, and $U=\varnothing$ is allowed with the empty covering.

source.place: Tags 075Y (lemma-check-lqc-on-etale-covering), proof first paragraph (replace the source stacks by scheme atlases and lift a test object etale locally), and 0764 (lemma-check-flat-comparison-on-etale-covering), proof (3), the same construction. Geometric inputs: stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06XH (lemma-surjective-flat-locally-finite-presentation), (2), and spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0CFV (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth).

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $a_j:W_j\to\mathcal X_j$ for every $j$, and a smooth surjective scheme atlas $b:V\to\mathcal X$, using [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Put $q_j=p_ja_j$. The diagonal representability in that definition and [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] show that each $q_j$, being a map from a scheme to $\mathcal X$, is representable by algebraic spaces. In particular $Z_j=W_j\times_{\mathcal X}V$ is an algebraic space. These choices use the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tags 026O (definition-algebraic-stack) and 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), (3)--(4); stacks-cohomology.tex Tag 075Y, proof first paragraph

proof.text: We verify smoothness without assuming $p_j$ representable. The projection $Z_j\to W_j$ is the base change of $b$, hence representable smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Its composite with $a_j$ is representable smooth by the same statement. The map $Z_j\to\mathcal X_j\times_{\mathcal X}V$ is the base change of $a_j$, hence representable smooth as well. Thus the diagram with top row $Z_j\to V$, bottom row $p_j$, and vertical maps $Z_j\to\mathcal X_j$, $b$, satisfies condition (A) of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion]; the assumed smoothness of $p_j$ gives smoothness of $Z_j\to V$. Now apply condition (B) of that criterion to the diagram with bottom row $q_j$ and vertical maps $Z_j\to W_j$, $b$. The first vertical map is surjective, so $q_j$ is smooth. Since $q_j$ is representable, the criterion's last clause says that every scheme base change of $q_j$ is a smooth algebraic-space morphism.

source.place: Tag 06FM (lemma-local-source-target), (1)--(2) and final representable clause, specialized by Tag 075U (definition-smooth)

proof.text: Form $W=\coprod_jW_j$ with its disjoint open-and-closed covering by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Stack descent on this covering [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] glues the objects $q_j$ to $q:W\to\mathcal X$: on distinct components the overlaps are empty, and on a component use its identity descent isomorphism. The map $q$ is representable by [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability] and smooth by source-open locality in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], since its restrictions are the smooth $q_j$. For any object $z\in\mathcal X(K)$ over a field, joint surjectivity first gives an extension $L/K$, an index $j$, an object $t\in\mathcal X_j(L)$, and $p_j(t)\simeq z|_L$. Surjectivity of $a_j$ gives a further extension $M/L$ and a point of $W_j(M)$ mapping to $t|_M$ up to isomorphism. Its composite to $W$ lifts $z|_M$. Thus $q$ is surjective in the stated field-extension sense, and hence on every scheme base change, by the chartwise calculus statement.

source.place: Tag 075Y (lemma-check-lqc-on-etale-covering), proof first paragraph: the disjoint-union smooth surjection; algebraic.tex Tag 045G; stacks-properties.tex Tags 04ZT, 04ZU

proof.text: For the given $x\in\mathcal X(U)$ form $P=W\times_{\mathcal X}U$. Representability of $q$ makes $P$ an algebraic space, and its projection $r:P\to U$ is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to $r$: obtain an etale jointly surjective family $e_k:A_k\to U$ and maps $v_k:A_k\to P$ with $rv_k=e_k$. By the explicit definition of the 2-fibre product in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], $v_k$ consists of a map $w_k:A_k\to W$ and an isomorphism $q(w_k)\simeq e_k^*x$.

Refine each $A_k$ by $A_{k,j}=A_k\times_WW_j$. Its projection to $A_k$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]; these opens cover $A_k$ because the component images cover $W$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Their composites $e_{k,j}:A_{k,j}\to U$ are etale by clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and jointly surjective because both successive families cover. Hence they are an etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The second projection $A_{k,j}\to W_j$ pulls back the atlas object to $y_{k,j}\in\mathcal X_j(A_{k,j})$; restricting the isomorphism from step 4 and using $q|_{W_j}\simeq p_ja_j$ gives $p_j(y_{k,j})\simeq e_{k,j}^*x$. This restriction is precisely functorial pullback of objects and isomorphisms in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Take $I=\{(k,j)\}$ and $j(k,j)=j$. All indices, coproducts, pullbacks and etale covers are taken within the fixed upper site universe, and then represented in its small skeleton [def-weil-size-convention]. If $U$ is empty take $I=\varnothing$ directly. In particular, if $J$ is empty, joint surjectivity precludes an object over a nonempty $U$ (restrict to a residue field), so this case is also covered.

Statement: it matches Stacks 075Y (stacks-cohomology.tex l.426-456) with 06XH(2) and 0CFV (spaces-topologies l.230-247). Joint surjectivity is field-point lifting after a field extension, which matches |X|=∪|f_j||X_j|. Nothing is weakened and no hypotheses are added. The parent lem-sfb-stack-lqc-flat-comparison-local-structure uses it exactly as stated. There is no re-split note for this item. Step 1: 045G source representability applies to q_j=p_j a_j because W_j is a scheme and X has representable diagonal. Step 2: Z_j->W_j is the base change of b; Z_j->X_j is a composite; Z_j->X_j×_X V is the base change of a_j. Criterion (A) for p_j gives Z_j->V smooth, then (B) with surjective Z_j->W_j gives q_j smooth. The representable clause gives scheme base change. Treating the scheme W_j as an algebraic stack is elementary. Step 3: gluing on the coproduct, smoothness by source-open locality and surjectivity through two field extensions all check against the chartwise calculus. Step 4: 0CFV node sections and the explicit 2-fibre product. Step 5: open-immersion refinement plus etale composition (1)-(2) and the site covering. Edge cases U=∅ and J=∅ are fine, and the refinement is needed because A_k may meet several W_j. uses ⊆ proof_deps with equal union. No SGA, no new nodes, no duplicates; the 0CFV/06XH hits are lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections, lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent, lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap and lem-sfb-stack-atlas-versal-completion, and none states lifts through a family of stack maps. Batch-5 flags: the three cited nodes reach sec-trace-formula only through the generic definition def-trf-algebraic-space, which is not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality. Accepted. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_object_lifts_of_smooth_stack_family {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (J : Type u) (Y : J → BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)) (p : ∀ j : J, BasedFunctor (Y j) X) (hX : IsAlgebraicModuliStack X) (hY : ∀ j : J, IsAlgebraicModuliStack (Y j)) (hp : ∀ j : J, IsSmoothModuliMap (p j)) (hsurj : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (b : Spec (.of K) ⟶ S) (z : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk b))) X), ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (i : K →+* L) (j : J) (y : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i) ≫ b)))) (Y j)), Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (y.comp (p j)) ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom i))))).comp z))) (U : Over S) (x : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) X) : ∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Over S) (e : ∀ i : I, V i ⟶ U) (j : I → J) (y : ∀ i : I, BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj (V i))) (Y (j i))), (∀ i : I, Etale (e i).left) ∧ (∀ z : U.left, ∃ (i : I) (t : (V i).left), (e i).left t = z) ∧ ∀ i : I, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso ((y i).comp (p (j i))) ((discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map (e i))).comp x))
